ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17, as amended, and Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations, SOR/2002-184; Criminal Code, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-46, s. 462.31; Canada Business Corporations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, s. 21.1 (register of individuals with significant control); Quebec Business Corporations Act, CQLR c. S-31.1, art. 33.1 (register of individuals with significant control); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. P-44.1 (Quebec enterprise register and declarations)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized certified copy of each director's and UBO's passport
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport issuing authority of the individual's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (1961) if the source jurisdiction is an HCCH member; otherwise consular legalization by the competent Canadian mission

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing for each corporate shareholder or parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registrar or equivalent authority in the shareholder's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization if required by Canada/Quebec receiving authority

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized proof of residential address of each UBO (utility bill or bank statement)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or regulated financial institution in the UBO's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarial certification and Hague Apostille / consular legalization as applicable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Sworn beneficial ownership declaration and due diligence questionnaire
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or commissioner for oaths in the UBO's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization to be recognized by Quebec notary and Registraire des entreprises

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, officers, shareholders holding 25% or more, and beneficial owners against (i) FINTRAC Politically Exposed Persons (domestic and foreign) lists; (ii) Office of Foreign Assets Control Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List; (iii) United Nations Consolidated Security Council Sanctions List; (iv) Canada's consolidated sanctions under the Special Economic Measures Act, R.S.C. 1992, c. 28, and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, S.C. 2017, c. 21; and (v) negative news and adverse media checks, with enhanced due diligence for source of wealth/funds and immediate suspicious transaction reporting to FINTRAC.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises, Government of Quebec online services (https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca), with cross-check of the NUANS database for federal corporate name searches via Corporations Canada/Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language, CQLR c. C-11, the name of a Quebec enterprise must be in French. A non-French name may be permitted only if it is a registered trademark or if an approved French form is also filed; names must be in Latin script, transliterated where required, and must include the appropriate legal element (Inc., Corp., Ltée, etc.).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: On a name-rejection notice, the applicant must first request the Registraire's written reasons. Within 30 days after the refusal, the applicant may file an administrative review request with the Registraire or seek judicial review before the Superior Court of Quebec under the Code of Civil Procedure, CQLR c. C-25.01, arts. 529 et seq., named 'Requête en révision judiciaire'. Where the rejection is from Corporations Canada for a federal CBCA name, a formal appeal to the Director may be filed under the CBCA within the prescribed filing window; concurrently, an amended name proposal can be resubmitted through both portals.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible only as a registered-office address if a physical service address in Quebec is maintained and the office is capable of accepting service of process and keeping corporate records. For a patent prosecution agency, a virtual office cannot replace the actual business premises required for professional licensing by Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (Canadian Intellectual Property Office) as a registered patent agent; a physical place of business and accessible records are expected.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 15% (moderate-low). Revenu Québec and the Registraire des entreprises may conduct unannounced checks to verify an actual place of business, especially for registered office providers, nominee arrangements, and professional/licensed agencies; the risk increases if the registered office is a virtual address or a common agent office.

Notarized UBO declarations, certified passport copies and corporate good-standing certificates for foreign shareholders

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notarial tariff and private service fees

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Quebec notary or business law firm
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for Quebec business incorporation; hourly or fixed fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under CQLR c. P-44.1

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Quebec), CQLR c. S-31.1; applicable sections include s. 3 (incorporation), s. 39 (articles), s. 191 (registered office), and ss. 115-118 (first directors' resolutions). If the federal form were elected, the Canada Business Corporations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44 would apply as an alternative; this dossier is based on the Quebec provincial incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec, Direction de l'immatriculation, 1200 Route de l'Église, Québec, QC G1V 4N1, Canada
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (statuts constitutifs) filed electronically through the Registraire des entreprises online portal, followed by issuance of a Certificate of Constitution and assignment of the Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow account are mandated under the QBCA. A corporation may issue shares for nominal consideration, e.g. CAD 1.00 per share; however, the full consideration must be received by the corporation before share certificates are issued, and directors may be jointly liable for shares issued without adequate consideration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the corporation subscribe to and accept 100 Class A common shares issued to the incorporator for full consideration of CAD 1.00 per share, to be paid in cash. RESOLVED that the registered office of the corporation be located at [full municipal address], Province of Quebec, and that the directors adopt the site as the registered address. RESOLVED that [Name] be appointed Chief Executive Officer, [Name] Secretary and [Name] Chief Financial Officer, each to serve until the next general meeting. RESOLVED that management be authorized to open corporate banking accounts, register the corporation with the Registraire des entreprises, Revenu Québec, CNESST and CPATA, and to execute any documents required for commencement of patent prosecution services.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name clearance and reservation under QBCA
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec – Corporate Name Service and NUANS search providers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation request to the Registraire des entreprises or obtain a NUANS report from an authorized service provider. Provide first and second proposed corporate names, include a legal element such as Inc., Corp. or Ltée, and ensure compliance with QBCA naming rules and the Charter of the French Language. Use the cleared name when drafting the articles.
required_dossiers: Proof of authorized name search or reservation receipt
Payment receipt for name reservation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or objected to, the registrar will state the grounds; the applicant may file a revised reservation using a different name or a modified name, or may apply to the court for a declaration that the name is registrable.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting of Articles of Incorporation and by-laws
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate legal counsel qualified to prepare and certify Quebec incorporations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft Articles of Incorporation in French or English setting out the corporate name, registered office address, share structure with rights and conditions, total number of directors, and any restrictions on share transfers. Prepare By-law No. 1, director consents, and the pre-incorporation organizational resolutions in accordance with QBCA Part III.
required_dossiers: Proposed share structure and class rights
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar identifies defects or omissions, revise and refile the articles within the prescribed time; missing consents may be executed retroactively under the QBCA and confirmed by an incorporator's or director's resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Articles of Incorporation and issuance of Certificate of Constitution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec – online filing portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the Registraire des entreprises online portal, upload the executed Articles of Incorporation, enter the initial registered office and directors, pay the incorporation fee, and submit for statutory examination. Upon approval, the registrar issues the Certificate of Constitution and a nine-digit Quebec Enterprise Number. The certificate is conclusive proof of incorporation under QBCA.
required_dossiers: Certified or electronically signed Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing is queried or rejected, correct the specified deficiencies and re-electronic-file. Where the rejection is final, the incorporator may file amended articles or seek judicial review in the Quebec Superior Court; filing fees paid are preserved or applied to the corrected submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First board organizational meeting and initial corporate resolutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of directors of the corporation; corporate minute book maintained at the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first directors' meeting after the issuance of the Certificate of Constitution. Adopt By-law No. 1, formally approve the allotment of shares, receive the subscription consideration, appoint officers, approve the corporate seal, adopt banking resolutions, appoint auditors or waive audit, and fix the fiscal year-end. Record the resolutions in the minute book and issue share certificates promptly.
required_dossiers: Minutes of the first meeting of directors
Consent of each officer to act
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a resolution is procedurally defective, the board may ratify it by a subsequent resolution and correct the minute book. Late share certificate issuance is cured by issuing the certificates and updating the securities register; ratification is available under QBCA provisions governing organizational resolutions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with Revenu Québec for TPS, TVQ, corporate income tax and employer accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Québec and Canada Revenue Agency business registration services
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation, complete the Revenu Québec business registration file to obtain the Quebec Sales Tax (TVQ) account, federal Goods and Services Tax (TPS) account, corporate income tax file, and employer source deductions file. The application must be filed within the statutory delay after becoming taxable or hiring employees. Payroll deductions must be remitted to Revenu Québec and Canada Revenue Agency.
required_dossiers: Corporate profile with directors' and officers' names
Registered office and place of business addresses
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registration is queried, submit the missing commercial or bank documents and activate the account retroactively; late registration penalties may be cancelled or reduced under Revenu Québec's administrative relief policy if the corporation demonstrates due diligence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Firm registration and agent licensing with CPATA and related professional requirements
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: College of Patent Agents and Trademark Agents (CPATA); Registraire des entreprises for business registration; Barreau du Québec if legal services are rendered in Quebec
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply to CPATA for firm registration as a patent and trademark agency, and ensure that each individual holding themselves out as a patent agent or trademark agent holds an active CPATA licence under the Patent Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. P-4, and the Trademarks Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. T-13. Provide evidence of professional qualifications, errors-and-omissions insurance, code of conduct compliance, and, if applicable, notification to the Barreau du Québec regarding non-legal IP services. The firm cannot practice before the Canadian Intellectual Property Office unless at least one member is a licensed agent.
required_dossiers: CPATA Individual Licence Applications for named agents
Notification to relevant Quebec professional bodies, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CPATA questions the application, provide supplemental resumes, insurance certificates or proof of good standing. Refused registration may be appealed under CPATA discipline or application procedures, or the firm may revise the application to restrict practice to types of services permitted by the proposed licence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Physical premises compliance, CNESST registration and municipal licences
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local municipal permit and building inspection department; CNESST; municipal fire safety department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify that the leased or owned premises are zoned for professional office use and obtain a certificate of occupancy. Secure municipal fire safety inspection and required occupancy permits. Register the corporation as an employer with CNESST before any staff are hired, and implement occupational health and safety measures, emergency evacuation plans and accessibility standards. Standard office use does not require an environmental impact assessment; if a laboratory or production workshop is later added, a Section 22 authorization under the Environment Quality Act may become necessary.
required_dossiers: Lease agreement or proof of ownership of premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipal permit or occupancy certificate is refused, remedy the zoning or fire-safety deficiencies and apply for reinspection. CNESST may issue notices of correction; promptly implement corrective measures and, where necessary, obtain a variance from the municipal zoning authority.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: College of Patent Agents and Trademark Agents (CPATA) for professional licensing; Registraire des entreprises du Québec for business registration; local municipal building and fire safety authorities for physical premises; CNESST for occupational health and safety
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: CPATA Firm Registration for Patent and Trademark Agency Services; individual Patent Agent Licence and Trademark Agent Licence under the Patent Act and Trademarks Act; Registraire des entreprises du Québec enterprise registration; municipal business permit and certificate of occupancy

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – Category 1 for general professional office use; no full EIA or authorization required. If the premises add a laboratory, printing/custom workshop or other industrial process, a new classification under the Regulation respecting the environmental impact assessment and review and an authorization under Section 22 of the Environment Quality Act may be required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: For office-only operations, there are no regulated process wastewater or VOCs. Where applicable, sanitary wastewater must meet municipal sewer discharge limits, air emissions must comply with the Clean Air Regulation (CQLR c. Q-2, r. 4.1), refrigerants must be handled by certified technicians, and electronic waste must be disposed through approved hazardous waste contractors.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain a fire safety certificate from the local fire prevention service, a certificate of structural and electrical compliance from the municipal building authority, and an employer registration with CNESST. For workplaces, implement an emergency evacuation plan, maintain adequate first-aid supplies, appoint a first-aid provider where required, and ensure that all premises, fixtures and furnishings meet the applicable occupational health and safety standards prescribed by the CNESST.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Federal: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) – online portal 'My Business Account' (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/e-services-businesses/business-account.html). Provincial: Revenu Québec – secure portal 'Cliquant' (https://www.revenuquebec.ca/en/online-services).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1. Incorporate federally under the Canada Business Corporations Act (or provincially under the Business Corporations Act (Quebec)) and obtain the certificate of incorporation or extra-provincial registration. 2. Apply to the CRA for the 9-digit federal Business Number (BN) using Business Registration Online or by filing Form RC1; select the required programme accounts: GST/HST (RT), payroll deductions (RP), corporation income tax (TC/RC), and import/export (RM/RE) as applicable. 3. Register the corporation with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec for the Quebec enterprise number (NEQ) and any provincial licences. 4. Register for the Quebec Sales Tax (QST), Quebec employer contributions, and provincial corporate income tax with Revenu Québec through 'Mon dossier institutionnel' in Cliquant. 5. For a patent prosecution agency, obtain patent agent registration with the Canadian Intellectual Property Office (CIPO) and comply with provincial legal requirements; this is independent of tax registration but is a precondition to lawful activity.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation – the corporation is generally a taxable Canadian corporation if incorporated in Canada; it is taxed as a separate legal person and is subject to federal Part I tax on worldwide income and Quebec provincial income tax on the portion of income allocated to a permanent establishment in Quebec. No pass-through treatment is available for this limited-liability corporation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election is available; entity classification follows corporate law and tax treaty context. Available elections include: allocation of the small business deduction limit among associated corporations using CRA T2 Schedule 8; election under Income Tax Act (ITA) s. 216 to be taxed on net Canadian rental income; election under ITA s. 217 in respect of certain non-resident employment income; and foreign affiliate elections under ITA s. 93 for deemed dividend treatment. Canada has enacted hybrid mismatch rules consistent with OECD BEPS Action 2; those rules operate automatically and do not confer an elective opt-in or opt-out.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (federal value-added sales tax) and QST (Quebec Sales Tax, a provincial VAT-type tax). Quebec does not participate in the HST; supplies in Quebec are subject to the 5% GST plus the 9.5% QST, producing a combined effective headline rate of 14.975% on the pre-tax selling price.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: C$30,000 for both GST/HST (worldwide taxable supplies) and QST (taxable supplies made in Quebec) over any four consecutive calendar quarters. Foreign suppliers making taxable supplies in Canada or Quebec must register when the applicable threshold is exceeded, even in the absence of a permanent establishment, and may use the simplified non-resident registration procedures if eligible.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not currently mandate real-time fiscal clearance, API transaction reporting, or a digital stamping regime. GST/HST registrants with annual taxable revenues greater than C$1 million must file returns electronically. Revenu Québec requires electronic filing of QST returns for registrants meeting defined turnover thresholds and encourages use of their secure online portal; standard XML formats are accepted for mass filing. No statutory nationwide continuous transaction control (CTC) e-invoicing obligation exists.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A supply of patent prosecution services may be zero-rated for GST/HST purposes under Part V, item 7 of Schedule VI of the Excise Tax Act when the recipient is a non-resident who is not registered for GST/HST and the service is not performed in connection with real property situated in Canada or tangible personal property situated in Canada at the time the service is performed. The QST regime contains an analogous zero-rating for exported services supplied in Quebec. The agency must maintain contemporaneous evidence that the recipient is resident outside Canada, the supply does not relate to Canadian-situated property under the statutory exception, and the service is genuinely consumed outside Canada.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (B3-3 / B3ECO) for any tangible deliverables, prototypes, or exhibits accompanying the service
Bill of Lading or air waybill for any physical cross-border shipment
Inward Remittance Certificate or equivalent bank confirmation (e.g., SWIFT MT103) evidencing receipt of payment from the non-resident client
Executed service agreement, commercial invoice, and engagement letter describing the patent prosecution services supplied to the non-resident
Non-resident status evidence of the recipient, such as a foreign corporate registry excerpt, declaration of non-residency, or relevant tax treaty residency certificate
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec may reassess a zero-rating claim and claw back input tax credits or refunds where documentary substantiation is deficient. Gross negligence penalties generally reach 40% of the tax avoided, with interest running from the date the amount was originally refunded or unreported. Misrepresentation may extend the normal reassessment period by up to 10 years. Fraudulent claims attract civil penalties and can lead to criminal prosecution under the Excise Tax Act (s. 327) and Quebec sales tax legislation, with fines and imprisonment available. Exporters should retain the full substantiation file for a minimum of six years, and longer in cases of prior misrepresentation.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (monetary authority and currency issuer); banking prudential supervision by Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI); AML/ATF supervision and wire reporting by FINTRAC. Canada does not maintain a separate Foreign Exchange Administration or exchange control authority.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is fully convertible for current and capital account transactions. Profit remittance, dividend distribution, interest payments, and repatriation of invested capital by non-resident shareholders are permitted without exchange-control approvals, subject to corporate law solvency restrictions under the Canada Business Corporations Act or the Quebec Business Corporations Act and to statutory withholding taxes. Cross-border funds transfers of CAD 10,000 or more must be reported by the financial institution to FINTRAC under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act. There are no restrictions on maintaining foreign-currency accounts with Canadian banks.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no mandatory surrender, repatriation timeline, or conversion ratio for export receipts. A patent prosecution agency may retain export-derived fees in the original foreign currency, convert them at commercial rates, or remit them abroad without central bank approval. Export receipts and cross-border service payments must be reported in the corporate income tax return, in balance-of-payments surveys when selected by the Bank of Canada, and through FINTRAC large-transaction and electronic-funds-transfer reports as applicable.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility, subject to material legal constraints. Offshore digital EMIs are not Canadian chartered banks and may not accept deposits or provide bank-guaranteed escrow in Canada. They may operate as money service businesses if registered with FINTRAC and, in Quebec, applicable money-services-business licensing may be required. Wise and similar EMIs are viable only for low-value disbursement and currency conversion rails; they are not acceptable as the sole clearing institution for patent office fee disbursements, client escrow, or capital injection accounts. A Canadian Schedule I bank account remains the mandatory primary treasury anchor.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Canadian banks do not generally require every director or shareholder to appear physically in branch. Remote account opening is commonly available upon completion of certified corporate documents, notarized identity documents, and a live video verification interview. For Quebec corporate accounts, a registered office address for service within Quebec is required, and at least the principal authorized signatory or a senior officer may be required to complete an in-person or video KYC interview. Non-resident directors must usually provide certified passport copies, proof of residential address, and a certificate of good standing or bank reference from their home jurisdiction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Frequent inbound wires from foreign patent portfolio owners and overseas associates with non-standard narrative fields
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed retainer agreements; itemized invoices matching WIPO/CIPO/foreign-office fee schedules; patent and trademark application copies; client KYC profiles; beneficial-owner declarations; corporate certificate of good standing; written explanation of funding sources; prior bank reference letters.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High velocity of outbound remittances to official patent offices and foreign legal associates without underlying commercial invoices
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Official fee receipt from CIPO, WIPO, USPTO, or foreign authorities; standing letter of instruction from client; disbursement ledger showing each payment mapped to a patent or trademark file; bank account purpose statement; regulatory attorney license evidence; FINTRAC registration status if applicable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Escrow or trust-account pattern where funds are received and disbursed without a clear profit margin or operating revenue
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Client-funded disbursement agreement; formal escrow terms clearly defining agency, not debtor-creditor, status; independent accounting ledgers showing no commingling; auditor or chartered professional accountant confirmation; corporate resolution authorizing escrow arrangements; Quebec privacy law compliance records.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO complexity with offshore holding companies or nominee shareholders not revealed in Quebec public registry
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full corporate transparency diagram; registered insurance/registry search from Registraire des entreprises; certified beneficial-ownership attestation; parent-company KYC packages; tax identification numbers for all UBOs; declaration of no PEP/sanctions status; notarized signatures from all required principals.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For equity capital injection from a foreign parent, the compliant rail is an inbound SWIFT MT103 wire to the corporation's Canadian operational account. The ordering bank must identify the remitter as the shareholder, and the beneficiary account is the corporate account at the Canadian Schedule I bank. Remittance field 70 should contain a clear reference such as 'EQUITY SUBSCRIPTION SHARE CAPITAL INV-YYYYMMDD'. Although Canada does not assign standardized payment purpose codes, banks may require classification under the BPM6 category 'Direct investment: equity capital' for regulatory reporting. The corporation must maintain the signed share subscription resolution, directors' resolution, updated share register, and Quebec business records. If the wire equals or exceeds CAD 10,000, the financial institution will file a large transaction report with FINTRAC; the client should be prepared to provide source-of-funds documentation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for patent prosecution and trademark registration should be executed by SWIFT MT103 payment orders for international settlements. For payments to CIPO and WIPO, the agency may use official electronic payment portals or bank-drafted wires. SWIFT MT103 is the appropriate instrument for fee settlements to overseas law firms, patent associates, and official offices; SWIFT MT202 is used only for interbank coverage. Commercial letters of credit are generally unsuitable for service-based IP fee payments and are reserved for trade in goods. Domestic CAD clearing should use the Large Value Transfer System (LVTS) or the newer Real-Time Rail (RTR) when necessary; low-value client refunds may be sent through Interac e-Transfer if below applicable limits and permitted by bank policy. All outbound wires require reconciliation to the underlying patent/trademark docket and official fee schedule.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CAD/USD and CAD/EUR forward contracts executed with OSFI-regulated Canadian banking counterparties for committed foreign-currency disbursements to WIPO, USPTO, and foreign patent offices
Plain-vanilla FX call or put options to cap conversion costs on projected foreign fee obligations without creating speculative exposure
Cross-currency swaps between CAD and USD or CAD and EUR where matching operational cash flows exceed a material threshold and hedge effectiveness can be documented
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) limited to illiquid currency pairs in jurisdictions where a deliverable market is unavailable, and only where a firm, documented exposure exists
Spot FX prefunding transactions as a routine treasury tool to align foreign-currency account balances with upcoming official fee payments, provided no open speculative position is retained

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada (Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual, within 60 days after each incorporation anniversary date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No fee for online filing; after 12 months of arrears, Director may administratively dissolve the corporation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual, within 60 days after the fiscal year end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late fees escalate; after 60 days, additional CAD 120; prolonged non-filing leads to strike-off of legal personality and cancellation of registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the fiscal year end (no later than the day ending 6 months after year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month (max 12 months); repeat offence applies 10% penalty; criminal sanctions for failure to file.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the fiscal year end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 5% late-filing penalty plus 1% per month up to 12 months; administrative interest compounds; unpaid instalments may trigger seizure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GST/HST Annual Return (if business exceeds threshold or voluntary registration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the fiscal year end for annual filers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 6% penalty plus 1% per month on unpaid GST/HST; late remittance fees up to 6% interest, monthly compounding.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory independent audit for non-public business corporations in Quebec or under CBCA if all shareholders consent to dispense with an auditor. An audit is required upon shareholder demand (holders of 5% or more of voting shares) or if the corporation is a reporting issuer.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (International Financial Reporting Standards) or ASPE (Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises) at the corporation's election; tax returns are prepared under Canadian Income Tax Act rules referencing GAAP with statutory adjustments.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: For CBCA corporations, the Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC) must be kept current, updated within 15 days of any change, and the federal annual return must confirm such register has been maintained. Quebec annual declaration requires strict accuracy of directors and shareholders data; any shareholding transfer must be recorded in the Register of Members and reflected in the annual declaration.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Combined general rate of 26.5% (federal 15% Part I general corporate rate plus Quebec provincial general corporate rate of 11.5%); a disputable federal 2.5% additional? No - headquarters federal rate is 15% net; combined headline rate as stated.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Canadian-controlled private corporations (CCPC) qualify for the small business deduction: 9% federal rate on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income, while Quebec applies a 3.2% reduced SME rate on eligible income (combined 12.2% incentive band). Additional incentives: refundable Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) investment tax credits (33.2% for qualifying CCPC expenditures; 15-31% general rates) and the Quebec R&D tax credit (20%-30% for qualifying R&D carried on in Quebec).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Federal T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (with Schedules 1-100 and related forms T106, T50, T2Schedules) filed electronically through the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) Netfile / EFILE service, mandatory for all corporate T2 filers; Quebec CO-17 Corporate Income Tax Return filed electronically via Revenu Québec's Espace client portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Both the T2 and the CO-17 are due six months after the corporation's fiscal year-end; balance-due payments are due two months after year-end (three months for a qualifying CCPC with an SBD claim), with quarterly instalments required when prior-year federal plus Quebec tax obligations exceed prescribed thresholds.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income for the fiscal period, including patent prosecution fees, government filing fee refunds, and investment income from retained official-office float balances.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations carrying on patent prosecution business in Canada must compute Canadian-source net income under Part I and allocate income to Quebec through the permanent establishment formula in force at the date of filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after capital cost allowance claims, loss carryforwards (20 years), charitable donations, and unapplied SR&ED balances.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim treaty-based exemptions only by enclosing a fiscal seat certificate issued by the foreign authority; treaty non-resident shareholders cannot claim SBD.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal tax at the general 15% rate or reduced 9% SBD rate, inclusive of provincial allocation of business income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the federal-provincial Income Tax Sharing Agreement by allocating taxable income to Quebec through Appendix A of the T2 Schedule 5.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T2 Schedule 1 (Foreign Tax Credits and International Transactions)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credits and disclosure of non-arm's-length transactions with non-residents, including cross-border IP royalty payments, bond interest, and intercompany management fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach T106 Information Return whenever aggregate non-arm's-length transactions with non-residents exceed CAD 1,000,000 (goods) or CAD 100,000 (services, rents, royalties, or other remuneration); produce OECD-compatible Local and Master File documentation upon CRA written demand.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec recalculated net income starting from federal net income with Quebec-specific adjustments for provincial R&D credits and contributory differences.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents with Quebec-source income complete Part 1 and attach a certificate of tax exemption if claiming relief under the Canada-Quebec Collection Agreement regulations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec taxable income after the deduction of non-capital losses carried forward up to 20 years and the small business deduction where properly claimed.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Quebec small business deduction is unavailable to non-resident corporations and to foreign-controlled corporations carrying on business only through an agency relationship.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of 5% of the balance owing plus 1% per complete month of late filing up to 12 months; repeat failure upgrades the federal penalty to 10% for a second occurrence; CRA daily interest accrues at the prescribed rate on unpaid tax; Revenu Québec levies the identical 5% + 1% per-month penalty plus interest on the CO-17; omissions of foreign T106 disclosures carry separate penalties of CAD 100 per day up to CAD 25,000.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Part XIII of the Income Tax Act applies a 25% withholding tax on dividends paid by a Canadian resident corporation to non-resident shareholders; Quebec does not separately withhold provincial tax on such dividends under the Federal-Provincial Tax Collection Agreement.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a reduced treaty rate (generally 15% for portfolio dividends and 5% for a shareholder owning at least 10% of voting shares in treaty situations): 1) the non-resident recipient must obtain a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from its home country tax authority; 2) the payor must secure the completed CRA treaty declaration form (Form NR301 series adapted for corporations, e.g., NR302) before the dividend payment is made; 3) the payor must date-stamp and retain the treaty file at its Canadian registered office for at least 6 years; 4) the treaty-reduced rate must be reported on the NR4 (Summary of Amounts Paid), on the Canadian T5 Supplementary (for federal purposes), and on the corresponding Revenu Québec RN-5? The system uses RL-3 where required; 5) a rejection by CRA after audit requires full 25% withholding retroactively plus daily interest.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties and patent licence fees paid cross-border attract 25% Part XIII withholding at the statutory level, with treaty rates commonly reduced to 10% (Canada-US Canada Convention, Article XX; Canada-EU treaties widely 10%); interest paid to a non-arm's-length non-resident lender is subject to 25% Part XIII withholding, but arm's-length interest is domestically exempt from Part XIII unless the interest constitutes 'participating debt interest'; under treaties, qualifying interest is often exempt outright or reduced to 10-15%.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory T106 disclosure is triggered when total non-arm's-length transactions with non-residents exceed CAD 1,000,000 (good transactions) or CAD 100,000 (services, rents, royalties, and other transfers); a Country-by-Country Report must be filed when the consolidated MNE group revenue is at least CAD 2,300,000,000; all other Canadian entities must contemporaneously prepare OECD-compliant Local/Master Files within three months of an audit demand and retain them for at least six years.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada applies GAAR — the General Anti-Avoidance Rule under s. 245 of the Income Tax Act (and s. 1075.2 of the Quebec Taxation Act) — which disallows tax benefits arising from avoidance transactions absent a genuine business purpose; no formal 'Economic Substance Regulations' exist in Canada, but CRA audit positions require real substance, including employees, premises, IP budgeting, decision-making functions and commercial foreseeability for a patent prosecution agency; shell holdcos holding patent prosecution intangibles without operational substance face reassessment and a 50% gross negligence penalty.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Wilful failure to file T2 or CO-17, under-reporting actual PCT filing fee income, fabricating deductible disbursements, falsely backdating invoices, or transferring profit to a non-resident patent-holding account while performing the prosecution work in Quebec.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Gross negligence penalty under s. 163(2) I.T.A. equal to 50% of the understated tax; criminal conviction under s. 239 I.T.A. carries a fine of up to CAD 200,000 and imprisonment not exceeding 2 years; Quebec Taxation Act s. 44 imposes provincial fines and impoundment of property connected to evasion; CRA may additionally impose 100% of the tax sought as part of disgorgement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers are jointly and severally liable under s. 227.1 I.T.A. for any unremitted Part XIII withholdings, GST/QST amounts, and payroll deductions whether or not collected; during evasion prosecutions, the court may issue travel bans, seize personal bank accounts, and sign restraint orders over residential real estate.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / GAAR (Lack of Economic Substance)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Interposing a Canadian shell corporation with no employees, no Quebec premises, no board minutes and no real security to hold patent prosecution IP and invoice royalty fees to foreign affiliates, while all material decisions remain outside Canada.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR reassessment cancels the claimed tax benefits and restores full taxable income, with arrears interest from the date each reassessed return was due; a 50% gross negligence penalty can stack where the sham arrangement was knowingly induced; the DTA benefits may be denied under the Principal Purpose Test embedded in Canada's tax conventions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be pursued under s. 160 I.T.A. for value taken out through an artificial pipeline; directors who personally orchestrated the GAAR scheme may lose the indemnification privilege of the corporation's insurance and be assessed personally where the shell is struck off or becomes bankrupt.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Funneling large client patent fees and government disbursement payments through Wise or official patent-office wire transfers without FINTRAC registration, failing to file a suspicious transaction report, omitting risk assessments, and not maintaining a written compliance regime for third-party patent-fee remittances in a low-risk but volume business.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative monetary penalties under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act of up to CAD 1,000,000 per violation and revocation of the money services business licence; criminal charges, upon conviction, may yield imprisonment up to 2 years where laundering and financing is proven; FINTRAC also publishes non-compliance assessments in the public registry.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Officers and directors who directed or authorized the breach are personally guilty of the offence and liable to the same penalties; in indictable proceedings, personal forfeiture orders, travel bans, and freezing of corporate bank accounts are used routinely by the Enforcement Bureau against responsible executives.
